procedural_matters: Based on SI 15.6, boats intending to request a hearing or request redress for an incident in the racing area shall radio their intention to the Race Committee, which NED 22 did.
SI 15.3 changes Rule 44.1 so that the Two-Turns Penalty is replaced by the One-Turn Penalty.
NED 22 was represented by Robin de Jong.
DEN 394 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b) at 17:24.
A crew member of DEN 394 arrived at 17:29 to explain that the helm was on his way. The hearing was suspended.
At 17:32 the hearing continued with both NED 22 and DEN 394 being present.
DEN 394 was represented by Soren Kaestel.
Mikko Jaatinnen (FIN 86) gave evidence as a witness for NED 22.
Gordon Davies gave evidence as a member of the international jury.
facts: Wind about 7 knots and choppy sea.
Approaching the windward mark on the second beat to windward: NED 22 and FIN 86 were on starboard and fetching the mark. NED 22 was to leeward, overlapped bow-to-bow with FIN 86 to windward.
DEN 394 was approaching the windward mark on port tack, on a converging course with NED 22 and FIN 86.
On the layline, 1,5 hull lengths away from the windward mark, DEN 394 luffed, passed head to wind and before being on a close-hauled course, was on a converging course with NED 22.
NED 22, half a hull length astern of DEN 394, bore away establishing an overlap to leeward.
When DEN 394 was on a close-hauled course, there was less than 1 metre lateral distance between the starboard side of NED 22 and the port side of DEN 394.
After sailing 1 hull length, just before the windward mark, DEN 394 luffed and immediately made contact with its port side and the starboard side of NED 22.
Right afterwards NED 22 touched the windward mark.
There was no serious damage or injury.
NED 22 and DEN 394 took a One-Turn-Penalty.

conclusions: After passing head to wind and before being on a close-hauled course, DEN 394 failed to keep clear of NED 22. DEN 394 broke RRS 13.
DEN 394 to windward failed to keep clear of NED 22 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
DEN 394 failed to give mark-room to NED 22, the inside overlapped boat, who was on starboard tack since entering the zone and was fetching the mark. DEN 394 broke RRS 18.3(b).
DEN 394 did not avoid contact with NED 22 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

It was not reasonably possible for NED 22, the right-of-way boat sailing within the mark-room to which she was entitled, to avoid contact with DEN 394 when it became clear that DEN 394 was not keeping clear and not giving mark-room. NED 22 did not break RRS 14(a).
DEN 394 caused contact between NED 22 and the windward mark even though it was reasonably possible to avoid causing it, and broke RRS 14(c).
Since NED 22 was compelled to break RRS 31 as a consequence of DEN 394 breaking RRS 11, 13, 14, and 18.3, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(a) for this breach.
decision: Since DEN 394 took an applicable penalty, she is not further penalized under RRS 60.5(c)(2).
Since NED 22 is exonerated by RRS 43.1(a) for her breach of RRS 31 no penalty is imposed on NED 22.
